question: Who sets drinking-water requirements and who normally treats and distributes municipal tap water in Canada?
generated_answer:
Drinking-water requirements are set by provincial and territorial governments. You can contact your local drinking-water utility to find out how your water is treated and distributed. You can also find out about the quality of your tap water by looking at the annual reports issued by your municipality. What is the difference between bottled water and tap water? Bottled water is water that has been packaged in glass or plastic bottles with a capacity of not more than 2,839 L (625 gallons). It can come from many different sources, including springs, aquifers, or municipal tap water supplies. However, unlike tap water, which is regulated by federal or provincial/territorial agencies, bottled water is not regulated regarding some of its quality parameters, such as those related to microbiological aspects. Bottled water may also be treated to improve its aesthetic characteristics, such as discoloration and off tastes. In contrast, tap water, which is usually treated prior to human consumption, is regulated by federal or provincial/territorial agencies regarding both aesthetic and health-related parameters. What are the different types of bottled water? In Canada, bottled water is classified into spring water, mineral water, and purified water. Spring water and mineral water are both bottled at the source. Mineral water contains a minimum of 500 mg/L total dissolved solids and a minimum of 250 mg/L calcium, magnesium and potassium ions. Spring water may not necessarily have a constant mineral composition; its minerals must be "naturally occurring," however. Purified water can be derived from either a spring or underground source, or it can come from municipal tap water supplies. It can also be treated using methods including reverse osmosis and ozonation, to name a few. Is bottled water safer than tap water? Currently in Canada, there is no evidence to support that bottled water is safer than tap water. Bottled water sources are routinely inspected, and testing is done to ensure that the water meets or exceeds health and aesthetic guidelines in order to prevent the growth of heterotrophic plate count bacteria. In contrast, tests are performed on tap water much more frequently to ensure that the water meets health and aesthetic guidelines. Does bottled water have health benefits that tap water does not have? Bottled water, just like tap water, offers no particular health benefits. The main difference between the two is that bottled water does not contain any dissolved minerals. Large quantities of minerals in tap water can sometimes affect the taste of the water. What are the ecological impacts of bottled water?

Bottled water has several ecological impacts, including those of producing, packaging, transporting, and disposing of the plastic bottles. In Canada, 3.4 billion plastic bottles are used per year, and only about 50% are recycled. The remaining bottles end up in landfills or in the environment as litter, which can then take up to 1,000 years to degrade. The production of plastic bottles also requires the use of petroleum, which is a non-renewable resource and a source of C02 emissions. What is the difference between hard water and soft water? Hard water has a high concentration of calcium and magnesium ions. These ions can precipitate out of the water and deposit as calcium carbonate (limestone) or magnesium hydroxide (dragon skin) in pipes, water heaters, boilers, and on bathroom tiles. In domestic situations, softening is generally done using an ion exchange water softener. The water becomes soft when the hardness ions are exchanged for sodium or potassium ions. Since the water now contains sodium chloride or potassium chloride rather than calcium carbonate or magnesium hydroxide, it will not be able to form scale deposits. What is the difference between temporary and permanent hardness? Temporary hardness is hardness that can be removed by boiling the water. Temporary hard water has a high concentration of calcium bicarbonate (Ca(HCO3)2). Boiling the water causes the calcium bicarbonate to be converted to calcium carbonate, which is then precipitated out of the water. The water becomes soft as it no longer contains calcium or magnesium ions. Permanent hardness is hardness that cannot be removed by boiling. Permanent hard water has a high concentration of calcium sulphate (CaSO4), which does not precipitate out of the water as calcium carbonate does. What is the difference between reverse osmosis and filtration? Filtration is the process of removing suspended solids from a fluid (such as water) by flowing it through a porous material such as ceramic, carbon, or polypropylene. The size of the pores in the filter determines the size of the particles that can be removed. Filtration typically only removes suspended solids, although some filters can also remove dissolved contaminants such as lead and chlorine. Reverse osmosis is a process that removes most inorganic particles and some organic compounds from water by forcing it through a semi-permeable membrane. Reverse osmosis can remove contaminants such as dissolved minerals, heavy metals, and bacteria. However, it cannot remove all contaminants, such as volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and some pesticides. What is the difference between distillation and deionization? Distillation is a process that removes impurities from water by boiling it and then condensing the steam. This process can remove dissolved minerals, heavy metals, and bacteria, but it cannot remove all contaminants, such as volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and some pesticides. Deionization is a process that removes ions from water by passing it through a bed of ion exchange resin. This process can remove dissolved minerals, heavy metals, and bacteria, but it cannot remove all contaminants, such as volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and some pesticides. What is the difference between a water softener and a water conditioner? A water softener is a device that removes hardness ions (calcium and magnesium) from water by exchanging them for sodium or potassium ions. This process makes the water softer and prevents scale buildup in pipes and appliances. A water conditioner is a device that removes dissolved minerals and other impurities from water, but it does not remove hardness ions. Water conditioners can be used to improve the taste and odor of water, but they do not make the water softer. What is the difference between a water filter and a water purifier? A water conditioner is a device that removes dissolved minerals and other impurities from water, but it does not remove hardness ions. Water conditioners can be used to improve the taste and odor of water, but they do not make the water softer. What is the difference between a water filter and a water purifier? A water filter is a device that removes suspended solids and some dissolved contaminants from water. Water filters can be used to remove impurities such as sediment, chlorine, and some heavy metals. A water purifier is a device that removes most contaminants from water, including dissolved minerals, heavy metals, bacteria, and viruses. Water purifiers can be used to make water safe to drink, but they are not always necessary for domestic use. What is the difference between a water distiller and a water deionizer? A water distiller is a device that removes impurities from water by boiling it and then condensing the steam. This process can remove dissolved minerals, heavy metals, and bacteria, but it cannot remove all contaminants, such as volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and some pesticides. A water deionizer is a device that removes ions from water by passing it through a bed of ion exchange resin. This process can remove dissolved minerals, heavy metals, and bacteria, but it cannot remove all contaminants, such as volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and some pesticides.
